candidate.title: Section 3 host pseudocode checks non-zero exit before timeout and omits the output bound, contradicting the normative classification precedence and the signal_death/nonzero_exit distinction
candidate.claim: This refines the iteration-3 candidate that was dropped for artifact shape only (missing Base-Commit/Target-File/Finding headers and no diff block); the underlying finding was never judged on merit and the text is unchanged at the pinned commit. The draft's Section 3 pseudocode evaluates `if status != 0: reject("non-zero exit")` BEFORE `if timed_out(child): reject("timeout")`, and contains no output-bound check at all. A host that kills a timed-out child observes a non-zero (signal) status, so a reader implementing the pseudocode literally classifies every timeout as nonzero_exit. The source contract §7.2 normatively orders the reported cause 'its own kills first (output bound, then timeout), then an unsolicited signal death, then a non-zero exit, and only then the stdout parse and schema checks' and says a host 'MUST NOT collapse' signal death and non-zero exit. An IETF reviewer will also note the pseudocode block carries no statement of its normative status, so a lazy implementer cannot tell whether the block or §7.2 wins. The fix is text-only: (1) add one sentence before the block ('This pseudocode is illustrative and non-normative; on any conflict the obligations in Section 6 govern'); (2) reorder the block to output-bound, timed_out, signal death, non-zero exit, then parse; (3) add the `if output_exceeded(child): reject("output_bound")` line so the pseudocode covers all four fail-closed families the conformance suite already tests (host-deny-oversize-stdout, host-deny-no-output-timeout, host-deny-killed-by-signal, host-deny-nonzero-exit-after-allow).
evidence: draft-kondoju-evc-01 §3 pseudocode: "if status != 0:                               reject(\"non-zero exit\")   // Sec 6\nif timed_out(child):                          reject(\"timeout\")         // Sec 6" — non-zero exit is tested first and no output-bound line exists.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2 (pinned 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92): "a host that reports *why* it failed closed (§16.3) **SHOULD** classify the cause it acted on in this precedence: its own kills first (output bound, then timeout), then an unsolicited signal death, then a non-zero exit, and only then the stdout parse and schema checks."

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: "death by an unsolicited signal and a non-zero exit are **distinct** conditions (`signal_death` vs `nonzero_exit`, §16.3) — a host **MUST NOT** collapse them into one classification."

Previous-iteration rejection record: experiment ietf-reviewer-pseudocode-unlabeled-normative-status-and-precedence failed the shape stage only ("missing Base-Commit header", "missing Target-File header", "missing Finding header", "no ```diff block"); no merit finding was recorded.

Conformance vectors host-deny-oversize-stdout, host-deny-no-output-timeout, host-deny-killed-by-signal, host-deny-nonzero-exit-after-allow (set 0.7.0) exercise the four families the corrected pseudocode must name.

candidate.title: §7.3 conditions reserve-before-act on host nonce mode, so a local-mode host may drop consume_nonces on the floor
candidate.claim: §3.2 states unconditionally that the host MUST reserve-before-act EACH consume_nonces entry, but §7.3 opens with 'When the host runs the verifier in host nonce mode … and receives allow with consume_nonces'. A host that believes it is in local mode (verifier owns the store) can therefore read §7.3 as not applying and ignore the list. Attack: a third-party `external`-kind verifier, or a misconfigured deployment where the verifier was started in host mode while the host thinks local, emits allow+consume_nonces without consuming locally; the host ignores the list; the proof replays indefinitely. Mode is an out-of-band configuration agreement with no in-band signal, so this misalignment is silent. Observable a vector can assert: HUT configured in local mode receives allow+consume_nonces twice; the second run MUST deny (i.e., presence of consume_nonces MUST trigger reservation regardless of configured mode).
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.2: "The host **MUST** reserve-before-act **EACH** entry (§7.3)." (unconditional)

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.3: "When the host runs the verifier in **host nonce mode** (§8) and receives `allow` with `consume_nonces`, the host **MUST** reserve **every** entry" (conditional on mode)
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.2: "Emitted only in host nonce mode (§8)." — a descriptive claim about the verifier, not a host obligation for the case where it is violated.
Vector index (set 0.7.0): all host-nonce-* vectors presuppose host nonce mode; none exercises a local-mode HUT receiving consume_nonces.
Pinned base: 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92.
candidate.proposed_artifact: A staged §7.3 diff making reservation mode-independent ('a host that receives consume_nonces MUST reserve every entry regardless of its configured nonce mode; a host unable to reserve MUST deny') plus a vector `host-nonce-local-mode-consume-nonces-replay-deny`.

score.reason: Both pinned hosts condition reservation on host mode, and Rust explicitly tests ignoring consume_nonces locally, confirming a concrete configuration-mismatch hazard addressable by requiring reservation or explicit denial.

candidate.title: Verifier MAY emit a trailing newline but host MUST reject 'trailing bytes': CRLF, double newline, leading whitespace and BOM are unspecified
candidate.claim:
§5.1 grants the verifier an OPTIONAL single trailing newline while §5.2 orders the host to reject any trailing bytes or leading/trailing prefix around the object. Read literally, a host that rejects `{"verdict":"allow"}
` is conforming (a newline is a trailing byte) and would deny every reference verifier that prints with println-style output; a host that tolerates arbitrary trailing whitespace is also conforming (it is not 'garbage'). Nothing decides `
` (Windows verifiers), two newlines, a leading space or newline, or a UTF-8 BOM (0xEF 0xBB 0xBF) which Windows PowerShell and some .NET streams prepend by default. A lazy host implemented as `JSON.parse(stdout.trim())` accepts leading whitespace, BOM-free CRLF and multiple newlines; a strict host rejects all of them; both pass the current 29 vectors because every fixture emits either the bare object, exactly one `
`, or clearly non-JSON garbage. This is the 'single most fragile part' of the contract and the framing grammar is not actually written down.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.1: "The verifier **MUST** write exactly one `JSON.stringify(verdict)` to the host-facing stdout, at the very end. A single trailing newline is **OPTIONAL**."

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.2: "The host **MUST** parse the verifier's stdout as **exactly one** JSON object with **no trailing bytes**, and **MUST** reject (treat as deny, §7) any of: stdout that is empty, not valid JSON, or contains a leading/trailing prefix or suffix around the object"
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5 heading text: "This is the single most fragile part of the implementation and is normative for both sides."

Conformance vector index (set 0.7.0): host-deny-allow-trailing-garbage and host-deny-leading-garbage use non-whitespace, non-JSON bytes; host-deny-signal-death-after-allow is described as 'newline-terminated'; no vector exercises `
`, `

`, a leading `
`/space, or a BOM before the object, so the whitespace/BOM boundary is untested in both directions.

RFC 8259 §2: 'Insignificant whitespace is allowed before or after any of the six structural characters' and §8.1: 'Implementations MUST NOT add a byte order mark ... In the interests of interoperability, implementations that parse JSON texts MAY ignore the presence of a byte order mark' — so BOM tolerance is itself parser-defined, which is exactly where two hosts diverge.
candidate.proposed_artifact: A spec diff to §5.1/§5.2 that states the exact framing grammar (the object, optionally followed by exactly one LF or CRLF; no leading bytes including whitespace or BOM; any other surrounding bytes are a fail-closed condition) together with two host_behavior vectors: host-allow-well-behaved-crlf-newline (positive control, expects allow) and host-deny-leading-bom-before-allow (expects deny classified stdout_malformed), each fixture reading stdin before writing.

score.reason: The pinned newline exception and no-trailing-bytes requirement leave framing unclear, while both reference parsers trim whitespace; bounded framing vectors should use the existing unparseable_stdout classification rather than stdout_malformed.

acceptance.reason: Rule 2(k) requires pinned-source verification before claims about repository code appear in artifacts, but this artifact explicitly includes an unverified claim about both reference parsers’ whitespace trimming.

candidate.title: Verdict `detail` is the sanctioned log channel but carries no secrecy or size constraint, unlike `message`
candidate.claim: Record-oriented competitors (AERF, authproof-sdk receipts, the CVA paper's request/policy-binding properties) define the decision record as something a third party can read and verify, so they constrain what a decision record may contain. EVC's deny verdict makes `message` MUST-NOT-contain-secrets but leaves `detail` as an unconstrained object that the verifier is told to populate with internal error context and that hosts will persist verbatim in audit logs. A verifier vendor can echo the raw bundle, a binding signature, or an operator key into detail without violating the contract; the only backstop is the host's output bound, which is sized for framing (the fixture floods past it), not for secret containment. EVC should extend the secrecy rule to detail, state that detail is host-log material that a host MAY truncate or drop without affecting the decision, and say hosts MUST NOT feed detail back into any authorization input.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.3: '`message` (string, REQUIRED on deny) — a one-line, human-actionable reason. It MUST NOT contain secrets.' followed by '`detail` (object, OPTIONAL) — structured context for logs/debugging. A verifier SHOULD echo the originating internal error code here'
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 verdict schema: '"detail": { "type": "object" }' with no properties, additionalProperties, or maxProperties constraint
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2 lists 'oversized ... stdout' as a fail-closed framing condition only; no text ties the output bound to secret containment
https://arxiv.org/html/2607.21325 (CVA: authorization soundness, principal binding, request binding, policy binding — decision artifacts are specified as third-party-readable)
https://github.com/Commonguy25/authproof-sdk ('signed, verifiable, tamper-proof delegation receipts for AI agents')
https://github.com/topics/agent-verification?o=desc&s=updated (AERF: 'tamper-evident, independently verifiable records of AI agent actions')
candidate.proposed_artifact: A staged prose diff against §3.3/§5.3 of spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md and the corresponding draft -02 section pinned to 9bf7544, extending the secrets prohibition to `detail`, declaring it non-authorization log material the host MAY truncate, and adding a matching Security Considerations paragraph.

score.reason: The pinned secrecy prohibition covers message but omits detail despite its designated logging role, making a matching prohibition and non-authorization clarification useful without changing the verdict schema.

acceptance.reason: Rule 2k is violated: the claimed reference-implementation limit of 'a few hundred bytes at most' contradicts pinned capabilities.ts, which echoes capability strings into detail without a length limit, and verdict.ts, which preserves them without truncation.

candidate.title: retain_until in the past (or ≤ 0) is schema-valid and licenses immediate eviction, so a replay is spec-compliant
candidate.claim: The verdict schema types retain_until as a bare integer with no minimum, and §3.2 only obliges the host to retain the nonce 'until' that value. A misbehaving classical/external-class verifier (or a compromised one) that emits `retain_until: 1` (or 0 / negative) produces a verdict the host accepts, reserves, and — per the letter of the contract — may garbage-collect immediately; the next presentation of the same proof reserves the nonce afresh and the action runs twice. This is a fail-open path reachable without any crypto break, purely through a lax integer. Set 0.7.0 asserts entry shape (host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type / extra-property / malformed-consume-nonce) but never asserts a value bound on retain_until. The observable: fixture returns allow with `retain_until` ≤ the request's `now_unix`; host MUST fail closed (schema_invalid) — or, at minimum, a second run within the vector MUST deny.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 verdict schema: `"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }` — no `minimum`/`exclusiveMinimum`, unlike request `now_unix` which carries `"exclusiveMinimum": 0`.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.2: "`retain_until` (integer, REQUIRED) — Unix seconds until which the host **MUST** retain the consumed nonce." — no obligation past that instant, so an already-elapsed value permits immediate eviction.
Vector index (set 0.7.0): host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type, host-deny-nonce-entry-extra-property, host-deny-malformed-consume-nonce — all shape checks; no vector bounds the retain_until value.
Pinned base: 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92.
candidate.proposed_artifact: A staged §3.2/§3.4 diff adding `exclusiveMinimum: 0` and a host MUST to reject `retain_until <= now_unix` as schema-invalid, plus hostile vectors `host-deny-retain-until-elapsed` and `host-deny-retain-until-nonpositive` with regenerated goldens.

score.reason: The pinned schema and prose permit already-elapsed retention timestamps without a host check, supporting bounded defensive validation and vectors, although neither reference store demonstrates immediate eviction and a compromised verifier remains trusted to decide authorization.

acceptance.reason: The Impact section explicitly requires implementation changes to hosted-verify, violating §2(f)’s binding prohibition on artifacts implying the hosted platform.
